lessons: Read SQUATCH_PLAN.md section 20 before writing anything. The fixture spec there defines the scenarios, the version-1 report schema, and escape attribution. This attempt took 12m of a 75m budget and missed all three.

bin/codex implement must write that scenario's canned file change into cwd (the worktree) before it prints agent_message. An empty diff can never merge. Key the author, implement and review answers by scenario, using the ticket stem or a marker in the prompt.
Test that the scripted implement call leaves a non-empty change in a temporary git worktree.

The escape defect must not be in the base app. Remove the machine-escape branch from app.py. Ship the escape as one named scenario ticket's canned implement diff, so it reaches main only through a machine merge that escape attribution can trace.

Rewrite both reports to the version-1 schema: origin self_diagnosed|player, summary, dedup signature, app commit/version, implicated paths (max 32), replay initial_state plus action log, and an optional log excerpt. The test must assert every field and the byte caps.

Guarantee zero spend inside the fixture itself. Add a launcher such as bin/fixture-serve that puts hosts/fixture/bin first on PATH, strips provider keys and execs serve. Test that shutil.which('codex') under that env resolves to the fixture script.
Do not leave the fixture root on sys.path or its app/replay modules in sys.modules. Use monkeypatch.syspath_prepend with delitem, or importlib spec_from_file_location under a unique name.

Keep the earlier lessons: parse the surface from the header and fail closed on unknown ones, match each surface's real contract, give exact byte counts, and create every replay file a report names. Change no engine module.
reason: Review found concrete fixable spec mismatches, each with a paved road; nothing shows the ticket is unsatisfiable or needs more capability, only that section 20 was not followed.
